messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point
function.description: Calculate the boiling point of a given substance at a specific pressure. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

substance.description: The substance for which to calculate the boiling point.

pressure.description: The pressure at which to calculate the boiling point. This is a float type value.

unit.description: The unit of the pressure. Default is 'kPa'.

message.content:
At 10 kPa (≈0.1 bar) the ice–water equilibrium temperature is only a few tenths of a degree above 0 °C.  
Using the Clausius–Clapeyron relation for the ice–water transition (ΔV ≈ 9.5 × 10⁻⁶ m³ mol⁻¹, ΔH ≈ 6.01 × 10³ J mol⁻¹, T ≈ 273 K) gives

\[
\frac{dT}{dP}\;\approx\;\frac{T\,\Delta V}{\Delta H}\;\approx\;0.043\;\text{K kPa}^{-1}.
\]

From the triple‑point pressure (6.112 kPa) to 10 kPa is a pressure rise of 3.888 kPa, so

\[
\Delta T \;\approx\; 0.043\;\text{K kPa}^{-1}\times 3.888\;\text{kPa}
          \;\approx\; 0.17\;\text{K}.
\]

Thus the freezing (melting) point of water at 10 kPa is about **+0.17 °C** (273.33 K).  

In practice, this is essentially 0 °C; the shift is so small that most laboratory measurements round it to 0 °C unless high precision is required.
